name: DeepEval

value: An open-source framework that treats LLM evaluation as unit testing. Test cases are pytest functions, assertions carry thresholds, and a failing faithfulness or relevance score fails the build. That framing is the point: it puts model-graded metrics and deterministic assertions in the same suite, so a pull request can be blocked both because a required field is missing and because groundedness dropped below the line. The metric library is the broadest of the open frameworks, covering RAG metrics, G-Eval for custom rubrics, and multi-turn conversational cases that score retrieval quality across a whole dialogue rather than turn by turn. A companion library adds red-teaming aligned to the OWASP Top 10 for LLMs and the NIST AI RMF.
engine: Python library, pytest-native. Optional hosted platform from Confident AI.
latency: Offline. Model-graded metrics cost judge calls per case; deterministic assertions are effectively free and instant.

quality: The most complete off-the-shelf metric coverage among open frameworks, and the cleanest CI story. Heavy judge usage on large suites can hit provider rate limits, which is a practical constraint on suite size rather than a defect.
tagline: Evaluation written as pytest, so quality failures break the build the way any other test does.
use_cases: Blocking a deploy when a quality metric regresses, in the same pipeline as unit tests
Mixing deterministic assertions with model-graded scores in one suite
Scoring multi-turn conversations where retrieval quality shifts across turns
Red-teaming for jailbreaks, PII leakage, prompt injection, and bias before release
integrations: OWASP Top 10 for LLMs and NIST AI RMF red-team mappings
governance_note: This is the cleanest answer to the audit question of how AI quality is controlled before release, because the evidence is the same artifact engineering already produces: a test run, versioned with the commit, that either passed or failed. Deterministic assertions deserve particular weight in that record. Model-graded scores are probabilistic and move with the judge, while an assertion that every response carries a citation, contains no PII, and refuses a prohibited prompt either held or did not. A defensible programme runs the deterministic gates first and treats the graded metrics as trend evidence on top, with the judge model pinned and recorded so scores stay comparable release to release.
training_optout: The library runs locally; judge calls reach your configured provider. The hosted platform receives whatever results you sync, under Confident AI terms.
